quotes.quote: Movement disorders were present in 32 (55%) subjects: 30 (52%) had ataxia, 14 (24%) had dyskinesia, and 9 (15%) had dystonia.
After being genetically confirmed with SSADHD, subjects enrolled in the natural history study undergo a series of clinical and laboratory assessments biennially.

Division of the total CSSs of our study group to quartiles showed that 13 subjects were found in the top quartile (CSS ≥ 19.25), indicating the mildest clinical severity (patients #1, #5, #11, #12, #16, #23, #35, #36, #37, #47, #51, #53, #54).

Succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD) (OMIM #271980) is a rare (prevalent in ~ 1/460,000^1) inherited metabolic disorder caused by autosomal recessive inheritance of ALDH5A1 sequence variants^2.

authors_classification.statement: Authors list c.755G > A among eight previously unreported variants, and make blanket statements covering all missense variants and all 32 cohort variants.

quotes.quote: eight of which were previously unreported (c.104_127 del, c.127delC, c.870 + 1G > T, 6p22.3 deletion, c.644_647delTGGG, c.1558G > C, c.755G > A, and c.1388del) (Table 1)

According to the computational predictive tools POLYPHEN-2, SIFT, and CUPSTAT, all missense variants were determined to have a pathogenic clinical significance (Table 1) in accordance with the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) standards and guidelines^32.
This study’s findings determined that the 32 allelic variants (eight of which are novel), present in 41 unique allelic combinations (Table 1) in 58 SSADHD participants, were pathogenic.

concerns: PMIDs 37503297 and 37962671 carry the same Research Square preprint text (DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-3111263/v1); 37962671 states a version was later published in Human Genetics. The two rows are one person counted once (same identity), not independent observations.

The person appears only as a numbered row in a genotype table of a natural-history cohort; there is no individual case description, sex, age or phenotype for this row. The cohort is 58 individuals from 50 families, so some rows are relatives, but the paper does not say which.
Zygosity is given only as a table label; the paper does not report parental testing or how phase was established.

Table 1 column alignment differs between the two text conversions: in 37503297 the value 0.13 and the word "tolerated" fall in separate cells, while 37962671 shows "0.13 tolerated" in the SIFT column. SIFT for this variant therefore reads 0.13 tolerated, while PolyPhen-2 reads probably damaging; the predictors disagree.
The Table 1 domain cell for c.755G > A is blank, while the Results text maps G252D to the NAD+ binding domain.
The authors' blanket statement for missense variants rests on in-silico tools only, and this variant has a SIFT "tolerated" call in the same table.
No transcript is stated in this paper.
notes_for_panel: A different change at the same codon (c.755G > T, G252V, homozygous in #46) and an adjacent codon-252 change (c.754G > T, G252C) are in the same cohort table; neither is this candidate.
